tools.name: propbank_lookup
tools.description:
Look up a lemma and every alternate of it in PropBank (at most 20 per call).

language is "en" or "zh". Returns Markdown: per lemma, every roleset with its roles and all
its examples (the sentence, then each argument; traces such as *T*-1 are PropBank's own),
or "not in PropBank". Lemmas over the limit are not looked up: the last line names them
(call again with them). There is no PropBank for another language (Uzbek): nothing.

messages.content:
## Input

Language: en
Document: en-0008, sentence 1 of 9

The sentence: its number, a tab, then its words separated by spaces.

1	Edmund Pope tasted freedom today for the first time in more than eight months .

content.content:
## taste

### taste-01 (use one's tastebuds, active perception of flavor)

- ARG0: taster
- ARG1: food

Example 1 (nasty trace chains): ``Parties are rather a state of mind, '' [she]-3 said, [*-3]-4 pausing only [*-4] to taste [*RNR*-1] and pass judgment on [the Georgian shashlik]-1 (``a little well done, but very good'').
- ARGM-DIS: only
- ARG0: [*-4]
- ARG1: [*RNR*-1]
- rel: taste

Example 2 (just arg1): Ms. Morgan is really insulting all the troops who 've been there to assume that by going for ten days and taking a few casual leisurely trips outside the Green Zone that she got a full taste of combat
- ARGM-EXT: full
- ARG1: of combat
- rel: taste

Example 3 (both args): Diminutive Vanderkitten Road Sprinter Starla Teddergreen pinned on the numbers for her first taste of mud racing
- ARG0: her
- ARGM-TMP: first
- ARG1: of mud racing
- rel: taste

Example 4 (LVC): Oh man , that is creepy . Farmers mkt sounds good ! They 're doing a tomato tasting ! What time are you thinking ?
- ARG0: they
- ARGM-LVB: doing
- ARG1: tomato
- rel: tasting

### taste-02 (possess a flavor)

- ARG1: thing with flavor
- ARG2: description of flavor

Example 1 (beautiful metaphor): They still buy apples mainly for big, red good looks -- that's why so many taste like woodchucks' punching bags.
- ARG1: so many
- ARG2: like woodchucks ' punching bags
- rel: taste

## free

### free-01 ((cause to be) available)

- ARG0: entity providing freedom, agent
- ARG1: entity made free
- ARG2: freed from
- ARG3: beneficiary/purpose

Example 1 (prepositional Arg3): But [the Oct. 17 temblor]-1 put a halt to much nonessential building , and heavy rains last week slowed the rest , [*]-1 freeing construction workers for earthquake repairs .
- ARG0: [*]
- ARG1: construction workers
- ARG3: for earthquake repairs
- rel: freeing

Example 2 (Arg3 as a VP): The New York Times Co. said [0] it reached a settlement with independent home delivery dealers in the metropolitan New York area that [*T*-1]will free the newspaper to expand home delivery circulation .
- ARG0: [*T*-1]
- ARGM-RCL: that -> a settlement
- ARGM-MOD: will
- ARG1: the newspaper
- ARG3: to expand home delivery circulation
- rel: free

Example 3 (with Arg2): Despite fears [0] the mine may be partially nationalized [*-2]by the new Namibian government following next month 's elections freeing the country from South African control , De Beers engineers are working [*-1] to extend the mine 's productive life for another 25 years , from the current estimate of 10 .
- ARG0: next month 's elections
- ARG1: the country
- ARG2: from South African control
- rel: freeing

### free-03 (costing nothing)

- ARG1: thing that costs nothing
- ARG2: "of charge" or similar

Example 1 (both args): The popcorn is free of charge when you purchase a ticket
- ARG1: The popcorn
- ARG2: of charge
- ARGM-TMP: when you purchase a ticket
- rel: free

### free-04 (unconstrained, unrestricted)

- ARG1: free entity
- ARG2: free from (former chains/burden)
- ARG3: resulting freedom (to do what)

Example 1 (args 1, 2): He is free from worry.
- ARG1: He
- ARG2: from worry
- rel: free

Example 2 (args 1, 3): She is free to read whatever she likes.
- ARG1: She
- ARG3: to read whatever she likes
- rel: free
